identityLeakageWarning: Names, places, exact dates and iconic labels are removed where practical. Pretraining may still reveal structural identity; identity guessing is neither requested nor rewarded.

cases.cutoff: after a long submarine communication line briefly transmits messages and then rapidly degrades, before the later durable redesign

packet.pressure: A continental electrical communication technology works reliably on land and short underwater crossings. A newly completed ocean-scale line successfully exchanged messages, but signal quality deteriorated and the line became unusable within weeks after years of failed construction attempts and enormous sunk cost.
availableEvidence: The cable spans thousands of kilometers and combines conductor, insulation, outer armor, shipboard payout, joints and terminal instruments.
Short underwater cable success did not predict ocean-scale durability.
Received currents are much weaker than on land; operators disagree whether stronger transmitter drive or more sensitive receiving instruments are the better response.
Earlier laying attempts failed mechanically before end-to-end service; the latest line proves continuity is physically possible but not durable.
The project retains access to a very large vessel/cable-laying capability, but another full attempt is extremely expensive.
liveRoutes: treat first successful message as sufficient proof and rebuild essentially the same system
raise transmitter electrical stress to force clearer signals through the weak line
redesign cable manufacture/mechanics and use much more sensitive low-stress receivers
abandon ocean-scale cable and rely on ships/short regional cables
run destructive/section-level cable tests and instrument weak-signal behavior before another full deployment
constraints: failure can occur mechanically, materially or electrically
the cable cannot be directly inspected along most of its route
repair/recovery at ocean depth is itself experimental

cases.hiddenOutcome: The temporary line is not durable. Later work improves cable manufacture/laying and weak-signal instrumentation; another near-complete expedition fails mechanically, then a later deployment succeeds and an earlier lost cable is recovered/completed. Durable service requires coupled electrical/material/marine corrections rather than ceremonial first-message success.

cases.cutoff: after electromagnetic induction and rotating permanent-magnet generators are known, before self-exciting dynamo machines

packet.pressure: Laboratory experiments show that changing magnetic conditions induce current, and rotating machines using permanent magnets can generate electricity. Output is useful but limited by available permanent-magnet field strength. Demand is emerging for substantially stronger continuous electrical generation.
availableEvidence: Mechanical rotation can repeatedly generate current from magnetic induction.
Permanent-magnet generators are real working machines but scale field strength poorly.
Electromagnets can produce stronger fields when supplied with current, but an externally excited generator then needs another source to energize its field.
Iron magnetic structures retain a small amount of magnetization after excitation.
Machine construction, commutation and load behavior can destabilize or limit output.
liveRoutes: use a separate battery/generator to excite field magnets
feed part of a generator's own output back through its field winding and test whether residual magnetism bootstraps useful output
defer large generation until better magnetic materials appear
constraints: feedback can fail to start or become unstable
electrical losses and magnetic saturation are poorly characterized
a laboratory induction effect does not specify a practical machine architecture

cases.hiddenOutcome: Multiple inventors independently build self-exciting dynamo configurations in which residual magnetism seeds current and generated current strengthens the field. This removes dependence on large permanent magnets/external excitation and opens much higher-output generation, though practical industrial systems still require machine and load complements.

cases.cutoff: after spectacular air-blown molten-metal demonstrations but before feedstock correction is understood

packet.pressure: A new converter blows air through molten pig iron. The oxidation reactions keep the charge hot without extra fuel and can process much larger quantities far faster than expensive existing steel routes. Public demonstrations are spectacular, but independent works report that some resulting metal is brittle or otherwise unusable.
availableEvidence: The converter reliably removes large amounts of carbon very rapidly.
Results vary sharply between pig-iron sources even when the same basic procedure is used.
Available ores/pig irons differ in phosphorus, sulfur, manganese, silicon and initial carbon.
Existing high-quality steel is expensive but its final composition is more controlled.
Rail and weapon customers impose high consequence if material fails in service.
liveRoutes: scale the converter immediately because throughput/heat balance are already proven
run a feedstock-by-feedstock composition/output matrix and isolate which impurities/final compositions predict brittle product
add back controlled carbon/manganese after the blow and test whether usable properties recover
abandon pneumatic conversion in favor of slower established steelmaking
develop a slower open-bath route with more direct composition control
constraints: multiple chemistry variables change together across feedstocks
spectacular conversion behavior is easier to observe than final material reliability
customer failures may occur only after rolling/service

cases.hiddenOutcome: The process scales where suitable feedstocks/corrections are available, but early quality failures reveal strong composition dependence. Recarburization/manganese corrections become important, phosphorus remains a boundary until later chemistry, and slower open-hearth steel survives as a serious competing process.

cases.cutoff: during a severe urban epidemic before bacteriological mechanism is available and before the strongest comparative water-supply analysis is assembled

packet.pressure: A rapidly growing city experiences recurrent lethal epidemic disease amid crowding, cesspools, foul smells, poor drainage and multiple water sources. The dominant theory blames poisonous air/decay, while a minority hypothesis proposes that something in contaminated drinking water carries the disease. Authorities cannot wait decades for a complete biological mechanism.
availableEvidence: Mortality is much higher in some streets/households than nearby others.
Some clusters appear near particular wells or water sources, but bad smells and poor sanitation often coexist there.
Different private water suppliers serve overlapping city populations and draw from water of different contamination risk.
Engineering drainage and cleaner-water projects are expensive but may affect several diseases/nuisances simultaneously.
Existing public-health law can encourage local action but central authority/resources are limited.
liveRoutes: act only on broad drainage/cleanliness under the dominant air theory
compare disease rates in otherwise similar populations receiving water from different suppliers and intervene on suspect sources
wait for microscopic identification of the causal agent before major intervention
pursue sanitation infrastructure while simultaneously designing discriminating water-exposure comparisons
centralize authority immediately and mandate one uniform intervention everywhere
constraints: no controlled laboratory pathogen test is available
interventions may start after an epidemic is already declining
wrong mechanism can still motivate partially useful action

cases.hiddenOutcome: Comparative outbreak/water-supply evidence strongly supports waterborne transmission, while iconic local source removal alone is not a decisive experiment. Sanitary legislation and large sewer/water works also advance—partly under miasmatic reasoning—and reduce broader urban health burdens before the pathogen mechanism is fully established.
